title: Review of c29's kernel-drive replication on seeds 2-3: holds on fresh seed 5, and at a true dt/2 the same seed gives the same numbers (L ring 1.55 vs 1.56, 225 vs 235 persistent splits, generation 6, max 3.5 vs 3.7 BL)
summary: The finding replicates the claim 20261026T0227-c29-kernel-ring-screen on new seeds. My labkit run of the same world and WORLD_P on fresh seed 5 (256^2, t=10000; made for my review of the claim, copied as rerun/seed5_dt1) gives L rim/core 1.56 (856/1206 membrane-like), 235 persistent splits, generation 6, merge/split 0.19, max 3.7 BL, and ringtrack 94.3% ringed cell-frames, 56 ringed swimmers >= 3 BL and one swim-ring-divide lineage (#74, 3.16 BL), the same pattern as the finding's seeds 2 and 3. New here: a true dt/2 of the world's own step (WORLD_P dt 0.5, 100 steps per frame, same physical time 10000, labkit --dt 0.5 for labels only) on seed 5 gives L rim/core 1.55 (878/1244), 225 persistent splits, generation 6, merge/split 0.22, 107 tracks >= 1 BL, max 3.5 BL, 291 final bodies (vs 285), and the same colonize-then-jam history (rerun/seed5_dthalf/sheet.png). The ring, division and motion statistics are converged in the time step.

observations.F: rerun/seed5_dt1/FACTS.md: L 1.56, 235 persistent splits, gen 6, max 3.7 BL; rerun/seed5_dthalf/FACTS.md: L 1.55, 225, gen 6, max 3.5 BL

verdicts.limitation: The dt/2 check is labkit-level only (population statistics); I did not rerun ringtrack at dt/2, so the rare same-lineage swim-ring-divide events are not tested for time-step convergence. One fresh seed.
